Hone a single craft, walk a single path, refine it, polish it,
and master it to the end—I will see it through. All for the sake of that fleeting moment of speed.

Ah... Grandpa.
Um... sorry for calling so suddenly.
...I was able to run fast.

I'm going to do my best with that Trainer.
...I really will. ...Yeah.

...1200 meters?
Sprint races... only?
Will you... accept this job with me?
...Get in. If it's my work you wanna see, look all you like.

Ngh?! Her pace isn't dropping at all—?!
Believe-san... to think you've come this far...!!

...Stake everything on the moment.
Pour every ounce in. That's all.
I see, that won't work!!

...I see. Understood.
I'll go get permission from my Trainer. —Let's do this.
(But I—the way I am now—!!)

Stop!! ...Pardon the sudden intrusion, Believe-san.
However, I would also like to request a practice heat. Would you be willing to accept?

Both Light O-san and I primarily run sprints.
Which means—we will be rivals moving forward.

Not yet. I can still hold on—!!
—Aaaaagh!!

I apologize for the sudden visit while explaining the situation. Believe's grandfather
silently gives a slow nod, then points toward the kei truck parked on the roadside.
...Amazing.
Yes. ...Thank you.

Unlike before, you must be doing sprint-focused training now.
Together with someone who looks like your new Trainer. That's why.

In that moment, watching Believe's eyes light up more innocently
than I had ever seen before as she watched her grandfather's work—

The "speed" Believe is striving for... that "speed" like her grandfather's.
It's a domain she can only reach if she commits entirely to it.

Uh, well... yes.
Why the sudden request, though?
Good. ...So, the one over there... you're—

Narrowing your field reduces the chances of glory. It eliminates options.
Restricting it strictly to 1200 meters does so even more. And yet—

It's completely natural for her to be surprised. The veteran trainers she had provisional contracts with before
would never have suggested such a path. And realistically, their approach was the sensible one.

To gauge where we all stand against each other...
What do you think? It's hardly a bad proposal, is it?

Watching his swift, unhesitating trowel work, and how the wall was
finished with flawless beauty without a single guide mark, the depth of his skill was unmistakable.

(I can concentrate.
...I can keep it up. At this distance... over this distance!)
My thoughts coalesce into a single conviction.

Gotta do it, or you won't get fast.
...Bein' fast is what matters most.
I want to entrust this to you.

It was the best yet. I... managed to do good work.
So—
Yes! ...—kh!!

And when I saw the craft he performed at the site we followed him to—
just as Believe had described, it was nothing short of magnificent.

(Light O-san's speed is second to none.
And Durandal-san's sharp finishing kick is formidable, too.)

To be frank, my understanding of plastering had amounted to
little more than "someone who applies plaster to walls," but—

Ah... Grandpa? ...Thanks for the other day.
Yeah. ...Yeah, I—

...Trainer.
So... um. Starting today—
I knew it... Grandpa really is amazing—!

TOOOOOOOH!!
Fastest! Fastest! MAX-I-MUM SPEED!!
Hmph...!!

A race against time. Swiftly, yet meticulously, before the plaster dries.
His intense concentration was enough to make even an onlooker forget to breathe—

Afterward, we were invited into her grandparents' home,
where I spoke with Believe once more. Yes, my thought was—

Having cleanly crossed the finish line ahead of both Calstone Light O and Durandal,
Believe then came over to where I was standing.

Believe. We want to run a practice heat with you.
Let's do it right away. Ready, start!

—And so, the next day. Seen off by her grandparents,
Believe and I returned from America to Japan's Tracen Academy...
